title: Equanimity
description: Twelve minutes with the eight worldly winds: praise and blame, gain and loss, pleasure and pain, fame and obscurity.

segments.say: Sit in a steady way, like a mountain. And close your eyes.
Feel the base of the body, the weight sinking down. Let the breath go on by itself.
The Buddha spoke of eight winds that blow through every life. Praise and blame. Gain and loss.
Pleasure and pain. Fame and obscurity.
No one escapes them. Not even the Buddha did.
Equanimity is not indifference. It is feeling everything, without being knocked over.
Let us feel the winds, one pair at a time.
Remember a time someone praised you. Feel what happens in the body.
Now a time someone criticised you. Feel it again.
Notice how the body lifts with one, and sinks with the other.
Say silently: praise and blame come and go. Neither one is who I am.
Now remember something you gained. And something you lost.
Gain and loss come and go. I can be present for both.
And think of a recent pleasure, and a recent pain.
Pleasure and pain come and go. I do not need to chase one or run from the other.
Now imagine the mountain. The wind blows from one side, then the other.
The trees bend. The mountain stays.
You can feel the wind, and still stay.
Now offer yourself these phrases, slowly.
May I accept things as they are.
May I be at peace in the middle of change.
May I care, without needing to control.
The wind will still blow today. Praise, blame, gain, loss.
Remember the mountain.
When you are ready, open your eyes.
